Janeese Lewis George

Democratic candidate for Mayor of the District of Columbia · Open seat

Ward 4 member of the Council of the District of Columbia; lawyer

Janeese Lewis George is a Democrat who has represented Ward 4 on the Council of the District of Columbia since January 2021 and describes herself as a democratic socialist. She announced her campaign for mayor on December 1, 2025, after Mayor Muriel Bowser said she would not seek a fourth term. She won the June 16, 2026 Democratic primary with about 53% of the vote, and runner-up Kenyan McDuffie conceded on June 18.

Where George stands

Housing
Proposes building 72,000 homes in five years, expanding rent stabilization, prioritizing affordable housing, reforming zoning laws and streamlining permitting.
Homelessness
Says her administration would not clear encampment residents without a stable path to permanent housing. Supports funding housing vouchers, including Permanent Supportive Housing and the Local Rent Supplement Program.
Federal intervention and home rule
Opposes the federal law-enforcement surge and National Guard deployment in D.C. She calls them an attack on the District's autonomy and has pledged to fight them.
Immigration enforcement
Proposes to scale back the Metropolitan Police Department's cooperation with federal immigration officials and the federal 'Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful' task force starting on her first day in office.
Autonomous vehicles
Opposes quickly legalizing autonomous vehicles such as Waymo in D.C. She says expected AI-related job losses put workers, including drivers, at risk.
Sanitation / rodent control
Says she and her team are preparing to tackle the District's rat problem directly, so that residents have safe and clean streets.

Background

  • Member, Council of the District of Columbia (Ward 4), 2021–present; elected 2020 after defeating incumbent Brandon Todd in the Democratic primary
  • Assistant attorney general, D.C. Office of the Attorney General under Karl Racine, starting 2014
  • J.D., Howard University School of Law
  • Graduate of D.C. public schools; third-generation Washingtonian
  • Won the 2026 Democratic mayoral primary (June 16, 2026)
